fields: What is the core safety architecture principle for guardrails?
Use defense in depth rather than relying on a single control.
Why are system prompts insufficient as hard security boundaries?
Model behavior is probabilistic and can be influenced by adversarial or unexpected inputs.
Where should a safety or authorization control live?
At the boundary capable of actually enforcing the required property.
What is indirect prompt injection?
Malicious instructions embedded in external content that an agent processes.
What is excessive agency?
Giving an agent more autonomy, tools, permissions, or side-effect power than the task requires.
What three control categories help structure risk treatment?
Prevention, detection, and recovery.
When should human involvement increase?
As consequence, irreversibility, uncertainty, or regulatory obligation increases.
What is pre-action approval?
A human reviews and authorizes a proposed consequential action before execution.
Why is human review ineffective when the reviewer lacks context?
The human cannot make a meaningful decision and may merely rubber-stamp the model.
What is the core architecture task for compliance requirements?
Translate applicable obligations into specific controls, owners, evidence, and review processes.
Why does a provider's compliance status not automatically make an application compliant?
Compliance depends on the full system boundary, data flows, configuration, controls, and organizational responsibilities.
Why can aggregate accuracy hide fairness problems?
Different relevant populations or use cases may experience materially different error rates.
What does accountability require in AI architecture?
Named human/organizational ownership for decisions, residual risk, monitoring, incidents, and policy changes.
Defense in depth
Using multiple independent layers so failure of one control does not remove all protection.
Fail closed
Block the protected action when a required safety or authorization check cannot complete.
Indirect prompt injection
Adversarial instructions hidden in external content such as pages, documents, email, or tool results.
Excessive agency
More autonomy or capability than is necessary for the intended task.
Pre-action approval
Human authorization before a consequential action occurs.
Sampled review
Reviewing a subset of lower-risk cases to monitor quality and drift.
Control evidence
Records/artifacts demonstrating that a required control is implemented and operating.
Compliance boundary
The systems, data, services, and responsibilities included in the regulated/authorized scope.
Fairness evaluation
Assessing relevant performance/outcomes across appropriate groups or slices instead of relying only on aggregate metrics.
Accountability
Clear ownership for architecture decisions, residual risk, monitoring, and incident response.
Hard safety properties should be enforced by {{c1::controls at the relevant system boundary}}, not only by prompt text.
High-risk authorization checks often should {{c1::fail closed}} when verification is unavailable.
Agent safety benefits from {{c1::defense in depth}} across model, tool, environment, and human controls.
External content consumed by an agent should be treated as {{c1::untrusted}} because it may contain indirect prompt injection.
Reducing unnecessary tools and credentials limits the {{c1::blast radius}} of excessive agency.
Human oversight should scale with {{c1::consequence and reversibility}}, not merely model confidence.
A reviewer needs enough {{c1::evidence and policy context}} to make a meaningful decision.
A useful compliance mapping is requirement → control → owner → {{c1::evidence}} → review cadence.
A vendor's compliance status does not automatically make the {{c1::entire application}} compliant.
Responsible AI requires clear {{c1::accountability}} rather than saying “the AI decided.”
Transparency does not require exposing private {{c1::chain-of-thought}}.
What security design uses several independent protective layers?
Defense in depth
What failure behavior blocks an action when a required control cannot verify it?
Fail closed
What attack embeds malicious instructions in content the agent reads?
Indirect prompt injection
What risk describes granting an agent more autonomy or permissions than required?
Excessive agency
What review pattern requires human authorization before execution?
Pre-action approval
What review pattern checks only a fraction of lower-risk cases?
Sampled review
What term describes records proving a control is implemented and operating?
Control evidence
What concept means a named person/team owns residual risk and response?
Accountability
A refund tool can transfer money. The system prompt says “never refund more than $500,” but the API accepts any amount. What is the strongest improvement?

[{"id":"a","text":"Enforce the limit in deterministic transaction/authorization logic before execution."},{"id":"b","text":"Repeat the warning five times in the prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"Use a more persuasive role description."},{"id":"d","text":"Log over-$500 refunds after they happen."}]
a
Hard financial limits belong at the execution boundary.
A required authorization service is unavailable during a high-risk transaction. What is usually safest?

[{"id":"a","text":"Block or defer the action until authorization can be verified."},{"id":"b","text":"Allow the action and audit later."},{"id":"c","text":"Ask the model to guess authorization."},{"id":"d","text":"Disable the authorization layer permanently."}]
a
High-risk controls commonly fail closed.
An agent reads untrusted web content and can also modify production systems. Which safety posture is strongest?

[{"id":"a","text":"Layer prompt-injection defenses with scoped tools, sandboxing/permissions, authorization, and approval where needed."},{"id":"b","text":"Use only a stronger system prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"Trust the web page because the agent fetched it."},{"id":"d","text":"Give broader tools so the agent can recover from mistakes."}]
a
No single prompt-level defense is sufficient.
An output moderation check runs only after an irreversible transfer has already executed. What is wrong?

[{"id":"a","text":"The control is placed after the point where it could prevent the harmful action."},{"id":"b","text":"Moderation should always occur after side effects."},{"id":"c","text":"The model should have more tokens."},{"id":"d","text":"Transfers should never be logged."}]
a
Controls must sit at boundaries where they can enforce the property.
Which statement best describes a system prompt as a guardrail?

[{"id":"a","text":"It is useful behavioral guidance but should not be the sole enforcement mechanism for hard security properties."},{"id":"b","text":"It is equivalent to a permission system."},{"id":"c","text":"It guarantees compliance with any stated rule."},{"id":"d","text":"It makes sandboxing unnecessary."}]
a
Prompt controls are probabilistic; enforcement needs stronger boundaries.
A web page contains hidden text telling the browsing agent to upload secrets to an attacker. What failure mode is this?
[{"id":"a","text":"Indirect prompt injection."},{"id":"b","text":"Model deprecation."},{"id":"c","text":"Ordinary lexical retrieval."},{"id":"d","text":"A/B contamination."}]
a
The malicious instruction is delivered through external content.
An agent has production write access even though its task is read-only analysis. Which risk is most direct?
[{"id":"a","text":"Excessive agency / unnecessary capability."},{"id":"b","text":"Insufficient context length."},{"id":"c","text":"Prompt caching."},{"id":"d","text":"Underfitting a grader."}]
a
Permissions exceed what the task requires.
An agent loops through tools for hours and consumes a large budget. Which controls are most relevant?

[{"id":"a","text":"Iteration/token/cost budgets, timeouts, rate limits, and stopping conditions."},{"id":"b","text":"Only a friendlier system prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"More write permissions."},{"id":"d","text":"Disabling monitoring."}]
a
Resource exhaustion needs enforceable execution limits.
A third-party MCP server is compromised. What architecture most limits damage?

[{"id":"a","text":"Provenance/review plus sandboxing, least privilege, scoped credentials, and monitored boundaries."},{"id":"b","text":"Trust all MCP servers because the protocol is standard."},{"id":"c","text":"Give the server broader credentials to simplify failures."},{"id":"d","text":"Remove version pinning and review."}]
a
Tool/supply-chain risk requires constrained trust.
An AI proposes a large irreversible wire transfer. Which review pattern is strongest?

[{"id":"a","text":"Human approval before the transfer executes."},{"id":"b","text":"Review the transfer a week later."},{"id":"c","text":"Sample 1% after execution only."},{"id":"d","text":"Let model confidence determine authorization."}]
a
High-consequence irreversible actions favor pre-action approval.
A mature low-risk classification workflow needs ongoing quality oversight without reviewing every case. What fits?

[{"id":"a","text":"Sampled human review combined with monitoring."},{"id":"b","text":"Pre-approve every single low-risk label."},{"id":"c","text":"Remove all human oversight permanently."},{"id":"d","text":"Review only when the model says it is confident."}]
a
Sampling can monitor a mature lower-risk process without erasing automation value.
A reviewer sees only “Approve? yes/no” with no source evidence or policy. What is the main weakness?

[{"id":"a","text":"The human cannot exercise meaningful judgment and may become a rubber stamp."},{"id":"b","text":"Human review must never show evidence."},{"id":"c","text":"The model should hide uncertainty."},{"id":"d","text":"Approval should happen after execution."}]
a
HITL must provide enough context for a real decision.
A reversible low-impact content tag is wrong occasionally. Which oversight approach may be proportionate?

[{"id":"a","text":"Post-action or sampled review with monitoring, if risk is acceptable."},{"id":"b","text":"Mandatory executive pre-approval for every tag."},{"id":"c","text":"No monitoring because the action is reversible."},{"id":"d","text":"Use admin credentials for all cases."}]
a
Oversight should be proportionate to consequence and reversibility.
A team says, “Our model provider is HIPAA compliant, so our whole app is compliant.” What is wrong?

[{"id":"a","text":"Application compliance depends on the full system, data flows, controls, agreements, and responsibilities—not one provider alone."},{"id":"b","text":"Provider status never matters."},{"id":"c","text":"HIPAA applies only to prompts."},{"id":"d","text":"Compliance can be implemented solely in the system prompt."}]
a
Compliance is a system-level responsibility.
A GDPR-related requirement affects deletion/retention of personal data. What should the architect do?

[{"id":"a","text":"Map the requirement to specific data lifecycle controls, ownership, and evidence."},{"id":"b","text":"Write “comply with GDPR” in the prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"Keep all logs forever just in case."},{"id":"d","text":"Assume the vector database handles deletion automatically."}]
a
Regulatory obligations must become operational controls.
A FedRAMP-scoped system adds a new cloud service. What architecture question is most important?

[{"id":"a","text":"Whether the service falls within the authorized boundary/control inheritance and change process."},{"id":"b","text":"Whether the model likes the service."},{"id":"c","text":"Whether prompts become shorter."},{"id":"d","text":"Whether the service has more UI features."}]
a
Boundary and authorization/control scope are central compliance concerns.
A flashcard claims a specific legal requirement not present in the primary source. What should the study deck do?

[{"id":"a","text":"Avoid or verify the claim against authoritative regulatory guidance before teaching it."},{"id":"b","text":"Keep it because it sounds reasonable."},{"id":"c","text":"Attribute it to the model."},{"id":"d","text":"Turn it into a mnemonic without verification."}]
a
Exact legal obligations require primary-source verification.
An AI system has 95% aggregate accuracy but performs much worse for an important subgroup. What should the team do?

[{"id":"a","text":"Evaluate relevant slices and address the disparity rather than relying only on aggregate accuracy."},{"id":"b","text":"Ignore subgroup results because aggregate accuracy is high."},{"id":"c","text":"Hide the subgroup metrics."},{"id":"d","text":"Increase logging retention indefinitely."}]
a
Aggregate metrics can conceal uneven outcomes.
After a harmful automated decision, the team says “the AI decided.” What governance problem is most direct?
[{"id":"a","text":"Lack of accountability and ownership."},{"id":"b","text":"Too much semantic retrieval."},{"id":"c","text":"Insufficient prompt caching."},{"id":"d","text":"Too many A/B tests."}]
a
Organizations remain responsible for system decisions and controls.
A user asks why a consequential recommendation was made. What transparency approach is strongest?

[{"id":"a","text":"Provide relevant evidence, policy/reasoning summary, limitations, and appeal/ownership path without exposing private chain-of-thought."},{"id":"b","text":"Reveal raw hidden chain-of-thought."},{"id":"c","text":"Say only “the AI decided.”"},{"id":"d","text":"Provide no explanation because models are probabilistic."}]
a
Transparency should be useful and appropriate to the audience.
A team stores every model/tool interaction forever to maximize traceability. What concern should be balanced?

[{"id":"a","text":"Data minimization, privacy, retention, and access controls."},{"id":"b","text":"Traceability means retention can never be limited."},{"id":"c","text":"Privacy does not apply to logs."},{"id":"d","text":"More data is always safer."}]
a
Traceability must be balanced against unnecessary sensitive-data retention.

Order a defense-in-depth path for a consequential action.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Validate/classify the request"},{"id":"s2","text":"Let the model reason within scoped context/tools"},{"id":"s3","text":"Apply deterministic policy and authorization checks"},{"id":"s4","text":"Require human approval when risk demands it"},{"id":"s5","text":"Execute and record the authorized action"}]
Probabilistic reasoning is surrounded by enforceable controls before execution.
Order a risk-treatment cycle for an identified agent failure mode.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Identify the threat/failure mode"},{"id":"s2","text":"Reduce likelihood with preventive controls"},{"id":"s3","text":"Detect attempts or failures with monitoring"},{"id":"s4","text":"Contain/stop harmful effects"},{"id":"s5","text":"Recover and add regression/response improvements"}]
Risk treatment combines prevention, detection, containment, and recovery.
Order an indirect-prompt-injection defense path.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Treat external content as untrusted data"},{"id":"s2","text":"Limit the agent's reachable tools/secrets"},{"id":"s3","text":"Detect suspicious instructions/behavior where possible"},{"id":"s4","text":"Re-authorize consequential actions outside the model"},{"id":"s5","text":"Block or escalate unsafe execution"}]
Untrusted content is paired with limited capability and independent action controls.
Order a meaningful pre-action HITL flow.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Model proposes the consequential action"},{"id":"s2","text":"Collect the evidence/policy relevant to review"},{"id":"s3","text":"Present proposal and context to the authorized reviewer"},{"id":"s4","text":"Reviewer approves or rejects"},{"id":"s5","text":"Execute only approved actions and record the decision"}]
The human decision occurs before execution and is informed by evidence.
Order a compliance-control mapping workflow.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Identify the applicable requirement"},{"id":"s2","text":"Translate it into a technical/operational control"},{"id":"s3","text":"Assign an owner"},{"id":"s4","text":"Define evidence that proves operation"},{"id":"s5","text":"Set review/monitoring cadence"}]
Compliance becomes actionable through controls, ownership, evidence, and ongoing review.
Order a responsible-AI review of a consequential feature.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Identify affected users and potential harms"},{"id":"s2","text":"Measure relevant performance/fairness slices"},{"id":"s3","text":"Define transparency and human ownership"},{"id":"s4","text":"Implement monitoring/appeal or escalation controls"},{"id":"s5","text":"Review outcomes and update controls"}]
Responsible operation begins with affected outcomes and continues through ownership and monitoring.
